title: hotfix(slo-enforcer): fix backoff thrashing during regional failover under load
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: prevent SLO enforcer backoff thrashing during sustained regional failover/load spikes; reduces unnecessary failovers and stabilizes SLO-based routing.
description:
Context: In a recent incident (SUP-3482) the SLO enforcer would enter a backoff/thrashing loop when a region experienced sustained high latency. Symptoms included repeated regional failover, aggressive load shedding, and oscillation between healthy and degraded states. This PR contains a targeted hotfix to stabilize backoff state transitions and add better hysteresis for regional failover decisions.

Root cause: The enforcer's backoff state machine used a single exponential backoff counter with no recovery window. When multiple upstream checks reported intermittent latency, the region would be pushed into backoff, then a small recovery signal would immediately reduce the backoff penalty, only for latency to spike again — resulting in thrashing. Additionally, regional failover decision logic combined short-window error rate and long-window latency incorrectly (weights reversed), making the enforcer overly sensitive to transient latency blips.

Fix summary:
- Introduce a bounded backoff with a minimum hold window (configurable) to prevent immediate flip-flops after short recoveries.
- Switch the failover scoring to use a weighted moving average where long-window latency has higher weight than short-window error spikes.
- Add a cooldown period after automated regional failover to avoid immediate re-failovers.
- Improve metrics and logs for backoff transitions to aid future debugging (new metric: slo_enforcer.backoff_state_transitions).
- Add e2e integration test that simulates sustained high tail latency and verifies no thrashing occurs.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover state transitions and new hold-window behavior.
- Integration test run in perf-canary validated stability under synthetic tail latency.
- Canary rollout to 10% traffic for 2 hours (observed stable routing, no repeated failovers).

Backport and risk: This is a hotfix; changes are scoped to the SLO enforcer subsystem and guarded by config flags (defaults enabled). Low-risk but high-impact for availability. Recommend backport to the last release branch if the customer experienced the issue.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added for backoff state machine
- [x] Integration test added to perf-canary
- [x] Metrics/logs added
- [x] QA smoke tests passed on canary
- [x] Approved by SRE and runtime owners

Commits summary: 3 commits —
- "slo-enforcer: bounded backoff + hold-window (hotfix)" — main behavioral change and config
- "slo-enforcer: adjust failover scoring to weighted moving average" — algorithm change
- "tests/slo-enforcer: add canary integration to prevent thrashing regressions" — tests and minor telemetry

Files of interest (high-level):
- services/slo-enforcer/src/backoff.rs — implement bounded backoff + hold-window (primary changes)
- services/slo-enforcer/src/failover.rs — scoring changes to use weighted moving average
- services/slo-enforcer/src/telemetry.rs — new backoff_state_transitions metric and logs
- services/slo-enforcer/tests/integration/canary_thrash_test.rs — synthetic latency test
- docs/ops/slo-enforcer.md — documentation updates for new config knobs
- charts/slo-enforcer/values.yaml — expose new config flags for rollout/backport

Small diffs (illustrative snippets):
- backoff.rs: introduced constants for MIN_HOLD_WINDOW_MS and MAX_BACKOFF_MS and logic to track hold_until timestamp.
- failover.rs: replaced naive short/long window weight (0.7/0.3) with (0.3 short, 0.7 long) and applied EMA smoothing.

CI: full test suite passed after re-run. One flaky lint failure on first run (unused import) was fixed in second commit.

Merge outcome: hotfix merged via squash-merge after approvals and canary validation. Deployment: rolled out to canary and then to main traffic with staged rollout policy.
